paragraphs.text: Should Parcelbird launch its own quick-commerce service in 2027?
Board discussion document, January 2027
Parcelbird
Board (two founders and two investors)
Board confidential; built from a synthetic briefing pack (fictional company and figures)

slides.title: Key questions

paragraphs.text: Key questions
Should Parcelbird launch Parcelbird Now, its own 15-minute grocery delivery service, in 2027 while reaching profit within its $12.0M of cash and keeping 12 months of runway?
Is quick commerce a market in which a new regional entrant can make money?
Can Parcelbird Now make money on each order once store costs are counted?
Did Columbus show the density and loyalty the model needs, at an affordable cost?
Can the launch be funded with 12 months of runway, and is there a better use of the cash?
What should Parcelbird do in 2027, and when would it revisit an own service?
Decision maker
Success criteria
Timing
Out of scope
The board (two founders and two investors)

A path to profitability within the current $12.0M of cash, with no new funding round; At least 12 months of runway at all times; Contribution profit per order by month 18, as the founders' model claims
Board meeting, January 2027
Cities beyond the three planned; A new funding round; The software product roadmap

slides.title: Executive summary

paragraphs.text: Executive summary
Do not launch Parcelbird Now in 2027: orders lose money on all the evidence and the plan breaks the runway floor; grow the software business instead
Quick commerce is growing fast, but neither incumbent has found a way to make money from it
–	QuickBasket closed 4 of its 11 cities in 2025
Each order loses about $6 at benchmark inputs; only the founders' plan, beyond the best site on four key inputs, makes money
–	Zipcart's fee fix would still leave a median store $1 short per order
Columbus has not shown the density or loyalty the model needs, and buying them would cost more than the cash
–	The pop-up averaged 280 orders a day, against a median of 900
The launch fails both board tests, while the software business can break even within today's cash if growth holds
–	Month 18 of the plan leaves about six months of runway, half the floor
Decide against the launch in January, fund four software hires and sell store-based fast delivery to grocers
–	Reopen the question only when customer sites pass four tests
